clue.text: Most unhappy person that may be seen on building site

definitions.text: that may be seen on building site

parts.note: blue means sad, so the most unhappy is the bluest
one is a person, as in 'one never knows'

explanation.surface: The gloomiest worker to be found anywhere on a construction site.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Person that may be seen' reads as one phrase, but the person ends the wordplay and the definition is the rest. Bluestone is a hard bluish-grey building stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Bluestone is a building material, so it is a thing you might spot lying about on a construction site.

clue.text: Footballer restored to team?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a defender in football
second meaning: returned to the side, as a player is after injury

explanation.surface: A player who has been brought back into the side after time out.
explanation.definitionFit: A defender is called a back, and a recalled player is said to be back in the team.

clue.text: A female in Paris with a number left in dining room?

parts.note: the French word for 'a' before a feminine noun
taken as written
ten is a number

explanation.surface: A Parisian woman sits with a numbered ticket, left waiting in a restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A female' sounds like a woman, but it is the word 'a' in its feminine French form. The question mark flags that 'left' means food untouched, not a person abandoned.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that is uneaten has been left on the plate, which is what happens at a dining table.

clue.text: Rested the first day of the weekend briefly

definitions.meaning: first meaning: past tense of sit, took a seat

definitions.text: the first day of the weekend briefly
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the short form of Saturday

explanation.surface: Someone took it easy at the start of the weekend.
explanation.definitionFit: To sit is to rest on a seat, and the standard abbreviation for Saturday is the same three letters.

clue.text: Decorated sumptuously in gold, awfully neat

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold

indicators.note: something done awfully is done badly, so the following word's letters come out in a mangled order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A room done up lavishly in gold, looking terribly tidy.
explanation.walkthrough: OR for gold comes from heraldry and is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornate describes something elaborately adorned, which is what being lavishly decorated amounts to.

clue.text: A feature of many a department store involving a real cost

definitions.text: A feature of many a department store

indicators.note: to involve is to entangle or wrap up together, so the following words get jumbled into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Something found in a big shop that costs a lot to install and run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Involving' reads as 'entailing' in the surface; here it signals the letters being tangled.
explanation.definitionFit: Large department stores commonly carry shoppers between floors on moving staircases.

clue.text: Leaves half blown away in meadow

indicators.note: half of the word being blown away means only its front half is kept

parts.note: taken as written; its last three letters go

explanation.surface: Autumn leaves, half of them scattered by wind across a field.
explanation.definitionFit: Lea is a poetic word for a grassy field or pasture.

clue.text: Drinks with added recreational drug — moral shortcoming

parts.note: an animal laps when it drinks with its tongue
E is short for ecstasy

explanation.surface: Mixing booze with party pills is a failing of character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drinks' looks like a noun but works as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapse is a temporary failure of standards, such as a slip in moral behaviour.

clue.text: Stop to have a breather around end of year

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: around means the breather phrase wraps itself about the next piece

parts.note: a breather is a short rest

indicators.note: end of tells us to take only the final letter of the following word

parts.note: the final letter of year

explanation.surface: Pausing for a breath as the year draws to a close.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrest something is to halt it, as in arresting a decline.

clue.text: Deceive with trick, concealing passion

indicators.note: concealing means the trick word hides the next piece inside itself

parts.note: a con is a swindle or trick
heat is intense passion, as in the heat of the moment

explanation.surface: Fooling someone with a scam while hiding one's true feelings.
explanation.definitionFit: To cheat on a partner is to deceive them by being unfaithful.

clue.text: King entertains primate in light-hearted event?

indicators.note: a host entertains guests inside the house, so the king holds the primate within

parts.note: CR stands for Carolus Rex, Latin for King Charles
an ape is a primate

explanation.surface: A monarch hosts a monkey at a jolly occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: CR for king is a crossword convention from royal monograms such as Carolus Rex.
explanation.definitionFit: A caper is a lively escapade or romp, a fun bit of mischief.

clue.text: They offer narratives and they may be liars

definitions.meaning: first meaning: people who recount tales
second meaning: people who tell fibs, as children are scolded for telling stories

explanation.surface: Narrators may not be trustworthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Telling stories means both recounting tales and, colloquially, lying, so both senses fit the same noun.

clue.text: Passionate deed — something changed in text

parts.note: red is the colour of passion and anger
a deed is an action

explanation.surface: An act of passion that alters a written document.
explanation.definitionFit: Redaction is editing or censoring a document, so it is an alteration made to text.

clue.text: Woman with aim to ensnare one

indicators.note: to ensnare is to trap, so the aim word catches the next piece inside it

parts.note: an end is a goal or aim
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A woman determined to catch a particular man.
explanation.definitionFit: Enid is a female first name, so it stands for an example of a woman.

clue.text: Fuss to be dealt with?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a commotion or bother
second meaning: still pending, as on a list of jobs

explanation.surface: A commotion that someone has to sort out.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the second meaning is two separate words rather than the hyphenated noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A to-do is a commotion, and things still to do are tasks awaiting attention.

clue.text: Merit being severed somehow

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified manner, so the letters are rearranged in an unstated way

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone earning reward for being cut off in some way.
explanation.definitionFit: To merit something is to be worthy of it, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Quarrels for left-overs?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: bits of food remaining after a meal

explanation.surface: Family rows breaking out over leftover food.
explanation.definitionFit: Scraps are both minor fights and odd remnants of food, two separate senses of one plural noun.

clue.text: One who's cut out to be an artist?

definitions.text: One who's cut out to be an artist?

parts.words: cut out to be an artist
parts.note: surface reading: someone naturally suited to a creative career
setter's reading: an artist who literally cuts lines into metal plates with acid or a needle

explanation.surface: A person born with a talent for art.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'cut out to be' means suited for; taken literally it describes an engraver of plates.
explanation.definitionFit: This printmaker incises designs into a metal plate, so cutting is the very craft of the art.

clue.text: Artist exaggerating could make a cur artistic

indicators.note: could make suggests the letters are reworked to produce something new

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An artist who exaggerates could make even a mongrel look stylish.
explanation.walkthrough: A cur is a scruffy dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartoonist of this kind draws people with features comically overstated.

clue.text: Prepared money

definitions.meaning: second meaning: cash, as in the informal 'the readies'

explanation.walkthrough: Ready money is cash in hand; in British slang the readies are banknotes.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready means set to go, and the noun is an informal word for available cash.

clue.text: Bird is cold, needing cover for head

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
a hat covers the head

explanation.surface: A shivering bird that could do with a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: The chat is a small songbird, as in stonechat or whinchat.
explanation.definitionFit: A chat is a type of small thrush-like songbird.

clue.text: Italian, a master seen in retrospect as fine instrument maker

indicators.note: retrospect means looking back, so the preceding words are read backwards

parts.note: IT is short for Italian, as in Italian vermouth
taken as written
MA is a Master of Arts degree

explanation.surface: An Italian virtuoso is recognised, looking back, as a great craftsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Italian' looks like part of the definition, since the maker was Italian, but it is wordplay. The Amati family of Cremona made violins.
explanation.definitionFit: Amati was a family of celebrated violin makers in Cremona, so the name stands for a superb luthier.

clue.text: Painter of house and courtyard

parts.note: HO is an abbreviation for house
a garth is an enclosed courtyard or yard, often in a cloister

explanation.surface: An artist who paints homes and their yards.
explanation.walkthrough: William Hogarth was an English painter and satirical engraver of the eighteenth century.
explanation.definitionFit: Hogarth is a famous English artist, so the name is an example of a painter.

clue.text: Travel round something sticky

parts.note: to go is to travel
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Getting about by avoiding something gummy.
explanation.definitionFit: Goo is a thick, viscous substance that clings to things.

clue.text: Speak, for example

definitions.meaning: second meaning: used to introduce an instance, as in 'pick a number

explanation.definitionFit: Say means utter aloud and is also used to introduce an illustration, like the phrase for instance.

clue.text: Most intolerant home in which there is a right bust-up

indicators.note: in which there is means the home word holds the rest of the clue inside it

parts.note: a nest is a home
taken as written
R is short for right
a row is a quarrel or bust-up

explanation.surface: The most bigoted household, where a proper fight has broken out.
explanation.walkthrough: A bust-up is a British word for a serious quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Narrow-minded people are intolerant, so narrowest means least tolerant of other views.
